cases.title: Comma-separated record with a name field
cases.why: Comma-separated values without spaces; the name is the first field and the commas are delimiters.

cases.title: Name and trade role under a header row
cases.why: A header row labels the columns Name and Role, so the second cell of the data row is the role even though it is also a surname.

ambiguity.note: The Name,Role header assigns the second cell to the role column.

cases.title: Quoted inverted name in a CSV row
cases.why: A CSV cell in quotes holds a surname-comma-given name; the comma inside the quotes is part of the name, the quotes are not.

cases.title: Name inside a JSON-style object
cases.why: Quotes and braces around a name in a key-value structure; the quotes are delimiters and not part of the span.

projections_excluded.reason: The projection wraps the text in another pair of quotation marks, which would nest with the quotes this case is about and change what it tests.

cases.title: Assignee label with a value that is also a bank
cases.why: An 'Assignee:' label usually holds a person, but the value 'Chase' is also a financial brand and the field could hold a team or vendor.

ambiguity.note: Assignee fields hold people, teams and vendors; the single capitalized value carries no further cue.

cases.title: Attn label with a committee whose name starts with a given name
cases.why: Partner of label-attn-person: the same label with a committee name that begins with a common given name.

ambiguity.note: 'Committee' is a group head noun, so 'Grant' is a modifier of the committee, not a person.

cases.title: Attn label with a person
cases.why: An 'Attn:' line is addressed to a person (or a department); here the two-token value is a person.

cases.title: City label with Charlotte as the value
cases.why: Partner of label-name-charlotte: the identical value under a City: label is the city.

cases.title: Country label with Jordan as the value
cases.why: Partner of label-name-jordan: the identical value under a Country: label is the country.

cases.title: Lowercase applicant line with a hyphen label
cases.why: A plain-text form line with a hyphen as the separator and all-lowercase content.

cases.title: Name label with Charlotte as the value
cases.why: The value Charlotte is also a city; the 'Name:' label says it is a person.

ambiguity.note: The key 'Name' selects a personal name.

cases.title: Name label with Jordan as the value
cases.why: The value Jordan is also a country; the 'Name:' label says it is a person's name.

ambiguity.note: The key 'Name' selects a personal name.

cases.title: Owner label whose value is a team named after a surname
cases.why: An Owner: label usually takes a person, but a value ending in 'Team' is a group; the head noun decides.

ambiguity.note: 'Team' is a group head noun; the label alone would not decide.

cases.title: Reviewer label with a title and name
cases.why: A label, a title and a name: the title is excluded and the label is not part of the span.

cases.title: Signature label with initials and surname
cases.why: A name written with initials, as on signature lines; the periods are part of the name span.

cases.title: Label-value line with a name
cases.why: Form-style 'Name: value' text with no sentence around the value.

cases.title: Name and role in a semicolon-separated record
cases.why: A record with several fields; only the first field is a person and the second is a job title that looks like a surname-ish word.

cases.title: Court caption with a person and a company
cases.why: A court caption separates parties with 'v.'; the first is a person, the second a company that reuses a surname.

ambiguity.note: 'Holdings' is a company head noun; 'v.' separates the parties.

cases.title: Actor name in a key=value log record
cases.why: A log line has no sentence grammar; the key 'actor=' and the two-token capitalized value are the only cues, and the value ends at the next key.

cases.title: Approver name before a ticket reference
cases.why: A semicolon-delimited record where the approver name is followed by a ticket id with a hyphen and digits.

cases.title: Name after a bracketed severity prefix
cases.why: A bracketed severity tag precedes a normal sentence; the capitalized tag must not be pulled into the name and the name starts after it.

cases.title: Lowercase name in a key=value record
cases.why: Machine-written records often lowercase everything; the key 'assignee=' says the value is a person even though capitalization carries no information.

cases.title: Name as the subject of a quoted log message
cases.why: A name inside a quoted msg field of a log line; the quotes delimit the message and are not part of the span.
cases.text: level=warn msg="Dana Whitlow failed login twice"

cases.title: Service name built from a surname
cases.why: A service= field whose value is a surname plus a component noun; the key marks a software component, not a person.

ambiguity.note: The key 'service' and the head noun 'Gateway' mark a software component.

cases.title: Class and method names in a stack frame
cases.why: A stack frame names classes and methods that look like surnames; dotted identifiers inside a frame are code, not people.

ambiguity.note: A dotted identifier followed by a file:line pair in parentheses is a code reference.

cases.title: Thread named like a person
cases.why: A thread= field holding a capitalized common-word name; the key marks a worker thread, not a person.

ambiguity.note: The key 'thread' says the value identifies a worker, not a person.

cases.title: Two names in adjacent key=value pairs
cases.why: Two names separated only by the next key; the first span must end before 'reviewer=' and not absorb the neighbour.

cases.title: Numbered list of names
cases.why: Item numbers with periods precede each name; the numbers and periods are not part of any span.

cases.title: Inverted name in a pipe-delimited cell without spaces
cases.why: A surname-comma-given name between pipes with no surrounding space.

cases.title: Reported-by field in a ticket
cases.why: A ticketing-system style field with a label and a full name.

cases.title: Greeting line with a name
cases.why: A salutation 'Dear X,' where the comma is part of the greeting format.

cases.title: Semicolon-delimited row with a city cell
cases.why: A name;city;role row where the city is a given name too; the semicolons carry no spaces.

ambiguity.note: In a name;place;role row the middle cell is the place.

cases.title: Sign-off with only a name on the final line
cases.why: A name alone on a line after a closing phrase: the only cue is its position in the message layout.

cases.title: Name beside a city cell
cases.why: A row where the second cell is a city that is also a given name; cells of the same visual shape carry different types.

ambiguity.note: Column position and the full-name cell next to it make the second cell a city.

cases.title: City column holding a city-like value
cases.why: A header row followed by a data row whose first cell is a city that is also a given name; the header names the column as a city.

ambiguity.note: The header 'City' labels the first column, so Savannah is a place and the Owner cell is a person.

cases.title: Name in a pipe-delimited table row
cases.why: A markdown-style row: a name cell, a role cell and a year cell. Pipes sit directly beside the span edges.

cases.title: Tab-separated row
cases.why: Tab-delimited cells have no space around the span; the tab is the only boundary.
